title: QESCO Bill Calculator 2026 (Latest Tariff) | Wattlyst
meta: Estimate your QESCO bill from units with the current tariff, FPA and all taxes. Protected and non-protected slabs explained.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: What is the QESCO per unit rate in 2026?
p: QESCO is the Quetta Electric Supply Company Limited, the ex-WAPDA distribution company for Balochistan. Its domestic consumers are billed on the uniform A-1 tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026, the same slabs that apply in Punjab, Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. For an unprotected home the rate of the slab the month reaches applies to every unit: 250 units are all billed at Rs 33.10.

The examples and the table below print the rate for each slab. The month's FPA, set by NEPRA and printed on the bill, is the only line not in the uniform tariff; add it in the advanced fields for the exact figure.

sections.h2: Why is a Quetta winter bill high?
p: Quetta sits high and cold; the heavy electricity months there are December to February rather than June to August. Where gas pressure is low, an electric heater, a geyser rod or an AC in heat mode carries the load, and a heater draws as much as an air conditioner. A home that used 180 protected units in autumn can reach 480 units in a heater month, and under unprotected billing every one of those units is charged at Rs 38.95.

The protected status is lost the same way: one month over 200 units, and the next 6 bills are unprotected. Balochistan has some of the strongest sun in the country, and the net billing calculator linked below shows what a rooftop solar system is worth against these slabs.

sections.h2: Does this QESCO calculator work for agricultural tubewells?
p: No. A large share of QESCO's load is agricultural tubewells, and those connections are billed on the agricultural tariff category with its own rates and a long-running subsidy and flat-payment arrangement between the federal and provincial governments. The domestic slabs on this page do not apply to them, and the page makes no estimate for a tubewell bill.
Shops and offices are billed on the commercial tariff and are also outside this tool. Use it for a house or flat with a domestic (A-1) connection, which is what the bill's tariff code shows.

QESCO serves the whole of Balochistan apart from Lasbela district, where Hub and the surrounding industrial area are supplied by K-Electric. That takes in Quetta, Pishin and Qila Abdullah in the north, Zhob and Loralai, Sibi and Naseerabad on the plains, and Khuzdar, Kalat, Kharan, Panjgur, Kech and Gwadar towards the coast. Wherever the home is, the domestic slab rates are the uniform national ones.

The printed bill, with the reference number and due date, is available from QESCO and through the online bill lookup by reference number; this page estimates the bill from your units and does not fetch your account.

faq.q: How do I get a QESCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from your bill, tick protected only if the bill says so, and add the FPA from the bill under advanced settings. For 250 units the estimate is Rs 11,284 before FPA.

faq.q: What is the QESCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab your month reaches: Rs 33.10 per unit for an unprotected home using 250 units. The table above lists the rate for every slab; protected and lifeline consumers pay less.

faq.q: What is the QESCO tariff for 2026?
faq.a: For homes, the uniform A-1 domestic tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026: lifeline slabs up to 100 units, protected slabs up to 200 units, unprotected slabs of 100 units each up to 700 and an open-ended top slab; connections of 5 kW and above are billed on ToU rates. Agricultural and commercial connections have separate tariffs.

faq.q: Is the QESCO tariff for tubewells the same as for homes?
faq.a: No. Agricultural tubewells are billed on the agricultural tariff category, and in Balochistan they also fall under a government subsidy and flat-payment arrangement. This calculator covers domestic connections only.

faq.q: How do I check my QESCO bill online?
faq.a: Through QESCO's online bill lookup by the reference number printed on the bill, which shows the current bill, due date and payment status. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your account.

faq.q: Does QESCO cover all of Balochistan?
faq.a: All of it except Lasbela district, where Hub and the surrounding area are served by K-Electric. Every QESCO domestic consumer, from Quetta to Gwadar, is billed on the same uniform slabs.

faq.q: Why is my QESCO bill higher than this estimate?
faq.a: Usually the month's FPA, arrears or a late-payment surcharge, or a bill that covers more than a month of readings. Add the FPA in the advanced fields; for a long reading period use the overbilling check linked below.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: A bill of Rs 25,000 or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: 7.5% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.

key_facts: QESCO, the Quetta Electric Supply Company Limited with its head office on Zarghoon Road in Quetta, bills domestic consumers on the uniform NEPRA A-1 tariff for 2026; the slab rates are the same as in every other province.
The QESCO per unit rate for an unprotected home using 250 units is Rs 33.10 on every unit, giving Rs 8,275 in energy charges before the fixed charge, surcharges and GST.
This calculator is for domestic A-1 connections only; QESCO's agricultural tubewell consumers are billed on the separate agricultural tariff and subsidy arrangements, which these slabs do not cover.
A QESCO home stays protected only while every one of the last 6 bills is at or under 200 units; in Quetta an electric heater month in winter can break the run as easily as an AC month does elsewhere.

The bill jumps at 700 units: up to there every unit is billed at Rs 41.85, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of Rs 47.20, which adds Rs 4,478 to the bill of an unprotected 1 kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Using this page for a tubewell or shop. The slabs here are the domestic A-1 tariff; agricultural and commercial connections have their own rates.
Expecting a Balochistan-only rate. QESCO bills the uniform NEPRA domestic tariff, so the slab rates match the rest of the country.
Ticking protected after a heater winter. Protection needs all of the last 6 months under 200 units, and one electric-heater month usually breaks the run.
Leaving the FPA blank when the bill shows one. The fuel adjustment changes monthly and can be a credit; copy it from the bill into the advanced field.

fields.name: units
fields.label: Units on the QESCO bill
fields.hint: Units (kWh) for the month, from the bill or from this and last month's meter readings. Domestic (A-1) connections only.

fields.name: sanctioned_kw
fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed on the bill; one to three for most Quetta homes. It sets the fixed charge.

fields.name: protected
fields.label: Protected consumer
fields.hint: Tick if every one of your last six QESCO bills was within the protected unit limit; the bill prints the category.

fields.name: lifeline
fields.label: Lifeline consumer (up to one hundred units)
fields.hint: Only for very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Monthly fuel price adjustment from the bill, positive or negative. Leave blank if unknown.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

examples.text: Energy charge Rs 2,095 slab-wise at protected rates, fixed charge Rs 300 for 1 kW, FC surcharge Rs 581, QTA Rs 93, GST Rs 552. Estimated QESCO bill Rs 3,621.

examples.title: 250 units, unprotected, no heating or cooling
examples.text: 250 units all at Rs 33.10 = Rs 8,275, fixed charge Rs 350, FC surcharge Rs 808, QTA Rs 130, GST Rs 1,721. Estimated QESCO bill Rs 11,284.

examples.title: 480 units in a Quetta winter with an electric heater, 2 kW
examples.text: 480 × Rs 38.95 = Rs 18,696, fixed charge Rs 1,000 for 2 kW, FC surcharge Rs 1,550, QTA Rs 249, GST Rs 3,869. Estimated QESCO bill Rs 25,364 before FPA.

examples.text: 60 units at the lifeline rate of Rs 7.74 = Rs 464, with no fixed charge and no QTA. With the FC surcharge and GST fields blank the estimate assumes neither applies to lifeline bills (still being verified): Rs 464.

content.answer: A QESCO home in Quetta or elsewhere in Balochistan using 250 units a month as an unprotected domestic consumer on a 1 kW connection pays about Rs 11,284: Rs 8,275 energy charge at Rs 33.10 per unit plus fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST. QESCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges + GST, before the month's FPA.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the bill
